reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Runs corehydro::numerics::support::run_callback (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/callback_runner.hpp), group "rng", method "probe": the runner seeds a MersenneTwister, hands the callback named by `construct.callback` a HANDLE on it (core/include/corehydro/numerics/support/rng_handle.hpp), and returns what the callback drew. The callback is written by each of the four runners itself as a native closure -- a C++ lambda, an R closure, a Python lambda, a C# delegate on upstream's own `(double[] parameters, Random prng)` Gibbs.Proposal signature -- so every case draws through a real host-language callback. THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS FILE: if a user's proposal or resample function drew from R's or Python's own generator instead of the one the run seeded, seeded results would stop being reproducible and would stop agreeing between the two languages, and nothing else in the suite would notice. Pinning the exact draws here is what makes the handle's stream an oracle rather than an assumption. `mt19937_reference_stream` carries genuine upstream literals: it is Test_MersenneTwister.Test_MT19937 -- the same int[] seeding, 1000 draws discarded, then ten NextDouble values whose expected numbers come from the reference mt19937ar.c output file -- transcribed verbatim with its 1E-8 delta. The other three cases have no upstream test literal (no upstream test seeds 12345 and reads NextDouble/Next), so their values are read off the REAL C# MersenneTwister through tools/oracle_emitter and are labeled EMITTER-READ. Neither kind is ever a value computed by this repo's own C++.

callbacks.Rng_Uniform: f(parameters, rng) -> parameters[0] draws of rng.uniform, the ported C# MersenneTwister.NextDouble
callbacks.Rng_Integers: f(parameters, rng) -> parameters[0] draws of rng.integers on [parameters[1], parameters[2]), the ported C# MersenneTwister.Next(minInclusive, maxExclusive)
callbacks.Rng_Interleaved: f(parameters, rng) -> 2 uniforms, 2 integers on [0, 100), 1 uniform, off ONE generator [corehydro addition: pins the draw ORDER, not just the values]
callbacks.Rng_Warmup1000: f(parameters, rng) -> 1000 uniforms discarded, then 10 kept  [the shape of Test_MersenneTwister.Test_MT19937]
